correctness.rationale: Betz–Fu–Masuda's Eqs. (47)–(54) give exactly the stated reduction at x=0 with c₃=v. The strict switch-probability order gives q₁p₂<q₂p₁ and hence u<v. For every root r of the logit equation, c₂ is a strict convex combination of u and v and Eq. (51) gives a unique admissible c₁; the construction is reversible. For F=β(G−d) the sign of F′ is that of (a+br)²−Kr(1−r), which equals [a−(2a+b)r]²+[4a(a+b)−K]r(1−r). This proves strict increase below and at equality, with at most an isolated stationary point at equality. If that point is the root at equality it is triple, without changing the distinct count. Above equality the positive function (a+br)²/[r(1−r)] diverges at both ends and crosses K twice, giving the displayed critical points. The logit limits and the increase–decrease–increase pattern yield the claimed one/two/three count including the two double-root levels. A supercritical threshold alone does not give three roots; d must lie between the two critical levels, as the record specifies. The boundary Jacobian has the triangular eigenvalues of Eqs. (55)–(58); its c₂ eigenvalue is −(a+br)r(1−r)F′(r). The middle branch repels in that scalar direction and is a saddle, not a full repeller, on the three-dimensional boundary. The rational witness satisfies the strict source-model inequalities; c(1/2)=13/19=−d/h and F′(1/2)=−1836/361. The other two roots bracket 1/2 and are tangent-attracting; their transverse linear growth rates have opposite signs, with exactly zero linear growth at the central root. This does not select a physical rare-invader branch. The supplied verify.py was inspected, not executed; its rational identities and bisections check the witness, not the analytic root count.

value.rationale: The source itself leaves open whether multiple candidate invasion calculations occur. The threshold and witness establish that the ambiguity can actually change the sign of a rare-invader prediction even if attention is restricted to conditionally attracting branches. The exact criterion tells when the boundary prescription is single-valued and when a separate branch selection question arises. The value is a diagnostic of this natural approximation, not a claim about finite-population fixation or multiple physical invasion probabilities.
